Today the ledger records no person\\u0027s name or account anywhere (docs/concepts.md: \\u0027GitHub confirms the person, and the ledger never records the account\\u0027). ProjectMembersCommand fills its Login column from the local OwnerDetails record for each root fingerprint, and only this node\\u0027s own owner exists locally, so every other member prints \\u0027unknown\\u0027. The member file the invite sweep writes (InviteSweepEngine.WriteMemberVouchAsync, members/\\u003Croot\\u003E.yaml) holds only role and issued_at. Each node already reads its own gh login and numeric id at join and daemon start (ProjectJoinCommand via NodeBootstrap.RefreshGitHubIdentityAsync; h9k owner show lists them), and a node with push mirrors the repository\\u0027s collaborators as read-only observations (ProjectGitHubMembers: AccountId, Login, Role). What is missing is the pairing of root fingerprint to login. Brian\\u0027s ruling: the joiner\\u0027s node writes its own login and numeric id into its own signed node file as a declared claim; the members table shows the declared login and cross-checks it against the collaborator mirror (declared login present with push reads confirmed, otherwise flagged). No prompt for a typed name: the gh login is the identity GitHub permissions already run on. Parked for later, not in this task: a verified pairing via GitHub\\u0027s published SSH keys (github.com/\\u003Clogin\\u003E.keys) matched to the node\\u0027s ssh-ed25519 key.
